episodes.label: The Word She Could Write — Pure Alexia From Déjerine & Landolt (1892) to Pre-/Postsurgical VWFA Word-Length Slopes, Visual Span Limits & Reversible Cortical Stimulation (2025)
episodes.notes: Cognitive neuropsychology and causal electrophysiology of pure alexia (alexia without agraphia): Déjerine & Landolt's (1892) classic clinical dissociation, Gaillard et al.'s (2006) longitudinal pre- vs. postsurgical left occipitotemporal resection (610 ms flat baseline -> 2,240 ms with +342 ms/letter slope), Starrfelt et al.'s (2009) reduced visual apprehension span across letters and digits (2.3 vs. 4.5), and Marchive, Angelini et al.'s (2025) reversible intracerebral stimulation inducing transient pure alexia with spared dictation.

episodes.label: The Skill His Hands Kept — Henry Molaison's Robotic Force-Field Motor Retention Without Declarative Recall, Post-1953 Semantic Learning & 3D Postmortem Hippocampal Histology
episodes.notes: Multiple human memory systems through quantitative testing of Patient H.M. (Henry Molaison): Scoville & Milner's (1957) surgical cohort, Shadmehr, Brandt & Corkin's robotic arm curl-field adaptation showing preserved motor-skill retention across days despite zero explicit recollection of the apparatus (Shadmehr & Krakauer 2008), O'Kane et al.'s (2004) sparse post-1953 semantic familiarity, and Annese et al.'s (2014) 2,401-slice histological brain reconstruction.

episodes.label: The Pupil That Followed Imagined Light — Acquired Aphantasia (Zeman 2010), Objective Pupillary Light-Imagery Reflexes (Kay 2022), Object vs. Spatial Memory Drawings & Narrative Pupillometry
episodes.notes: Physiological and behavioral measurement of visual mental imagery: Zeman et al.'s (2010) patient MX with acquired loss of voluntary imagery despite intact visual-perceptual tasks, Kay et al.'s (2022) pupillary constriction/dilation to imagined bright vs. dark triangles scaling with vividness and absent in aphantasia, Bainbridge et al.'s (2021) scene-drawing dissociation of object detail from intact spatial layout, and Vanbuckhave et al.'s (2026) spoken-story pupillometry.

episodes.label: The Face That Changed in Place — Intracranial Fusiform Stimulation Metamorphopsia (Parvizi 2012), Facephenes & Rainbows (Schalk 2017) & Millisecond Ventral-Stream Dynamics
episodes.notes: Causal intracranial electrophysiology of human face perception: Parvizi et al.'s (2012) sham-controlled fusiform gyrus electrical stimulation inducing selective real-face distortion, Schalk et al.'s (2017) illusory 'facephenes' vs. chromatic rainbows across adjacent ventral-temporal electrodes, Keller et al. (2017), and Schrouff et al.'s (2020) fast ECoG temporal dynamics.

episodes.label: Reflexes, Recall, and Four Plastic Tubes — Bedside Neurologic Localization & HINTS vs. Early MRI (H053), Cognitive & Neuropsychological Storage-vs-Retrieval Profiling (H054) & Lumbar Puncture, 4-Tube Xanthochromia & CSF Signatures (H055)
episodes.notes: Clinical Cluster & Clinical Neuroscience synthesis of standardized neurologic localization (H053), neuropsychological profiling (H054), and CSF analysis (H055): forehead-sparing CN VII, Romberg proprioception, FOUR Score, HINTS beating early DWI MRI, and Hoover sign; CVLT-3 storage vs. retrieval rescue, DLB haloperidol ban, TOPF norms, and TOMM validity; and Hasbun pre-LP CT + immediate antibiotics, 450-460 nm xanthochromia, CSF lactate, <72h HSV-1 PCR traps, and Lancet 2018 atraumatic needles (n=31,412).

episodes.label: Can a God Be Fooled? — Developmental False-Belief Tasks, Barrett's Cracker Box, Yukatek Maya Interviews & Omniscience vs. Moral Policing
episodes.notes: Developmental cognitive science of supernatural minds: unexpected-contents false-belief tasks (Barrett et al. 2001; Knight et al. Yukatek Maya; Lane et al. preparedness vs. anthropomorphism) and separating epistemic omniscience from moral policing across development.

episodes.label: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
episodes.notes: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

episodes.label: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
episodes.notes: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

episodes.label: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
episodes.notes: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

episodes.label: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
episodes.notes: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

episodes.label: The Days After the Bleed — Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal SAH, Dihydropyridine Cav1.2 Fenestration Binding (PDB 5KMF / 8HMB), Pickard British Aneurysm Nimodipine Trial & Wrong-Route IV Boxed Warning
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 89: Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal SAH, Dihydropyridine Cav1.2 Fenestration Binding (PDB 5KMF / 8HMB), Pickard British Aneurysm Nimodipine Trial & Wrong-Route IV Boxed Warning. Six days after a ruptured aneurysm is secured, a woman who was speaking clearly can no longer name a key. The Critical Care Clinician follows her exam, arterial pressure and cerebral circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows nimodipine from a Bayer patent into a membrane pocket, then asks which human outcomes changed. The case, values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook chapter “Voltage-Gated Calcium Channel Antagonists for the Central Nervous System” (2010) provides channel taxonomy through its Table 1 entry for CaV1.2/α1C. Primary studies supply the nimodipine evidence. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: When the Pour Stood Still — Cerebral Akinetopsia in Patient L.M., Random-Dot Signal-to-Noise Breakdown (Baker 1991), Post-Stroke Smooth-Pursuit Eye Tracking & Speed-Selective Reversal
episodes.notes: Selective loss and dissociation of human visual motion processing: Zihl & Heywood's (2015) clinical synthesis of bilateral V5/MT+ lesion patient L.M. ('frozen tea'), Baker et al.'s (1991) random-dot kinematogram demonstration of intact low-noise direction discrimination collapsing under visual noise, Cooper et al.'s (2012) unilateral stroke eye-tracking dissociation, and Heutink et al.'s (2019) patient T.D. speed-dependent motion reversal.

episodes.label: How a Single Thalamic Artery Switches Off Consciousness
episodes.notes: Neurological and vascular investigation of acute bilateral paramedian thalamic infarction. Analyzes the anatomical occlusion of the artery of Percheron and its immediate disruption of ascending reticular activating system networks.

episodes.label: Covert Consciousness and Playing Tennis in a Coma
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of cognitive motor dissociation in patients diagnosed with persistent vegetative states. Evaluates the use of functional neuroimaging to detect covert consciousness through mental imagery tasks, such as playing tennis, to redefine the boundaries of clinical coma and neural recovery.

episodes.label: Waking Up Paralyzed Under General Anesthesia
episodes.notes: Pharmacological and neurophysiological dissection of intraoperative awareness during neuromuscular blockade with rocuronium. Utilizes the isolated forearm technique to investigate the clinical boundaries of consciousness and the terrifying biophysics of being wide awake yet paralyzed under the scalpel during general anesthesia.

episodes.label: Two Minds in One Skull and Split Brain Secrets
episodes.notes: Neuropsychological investigation of corpus callosotomy patients and hemispheric lateralization. Analyzes Gazzaniga's split-brain experiments, interpreter theory, and the dissociation of conscious agency across surgically severed cerebral pathways.

episodes.label: Autoimmune Psychosis and Anti NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
episodes.notes: Clinical and immunopathological dissection of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis triggered by paraneoplastic ovarian teratomas. Synthesizes cerebrospinal fluid analysis with neuroimaging to differentiate autoimmune psychosis from primary psychiatric disorders, highlighting the molecular mechanisms of receptor internalisation and recovery.

episodes.label: ICU Red-Alert Orders — Shock Gaps, Ventilator Curves & Coma EEG
episodes.notes: Clinical and biochemical reconstruction of critical care diagnostics involving Stewart strong ion gaps, ventilator waveform analysis, and thromboelastography. Evaluates the utility of continuous ICU video-EEG in unmasking silent non-convulsive status epilepticus and the biophysical limits of scalp electrodes in recording cortical potentials.

episodes.label: The Neurodiagnostic Vault — 10-20 EEG, Single-Fiber EMG Jitter, Evoked Potentials & RT-QuIC
episodes.notes: Clinical neurodiagnostic audit of International 10-20 electroencephalography patterns, single-fiber electromyography jitter, and evoked potentials. Examines advanced laboratory cerebrospinal fluid assays including real-time quaking-induced conversion for prion detection and central nervous system disorders.

episodes.label: Confessions of a Peroxidized Lipid in Status Epilepticus
episodes.notes: Biophysical reconstruction of ferroptotic membrane failure and lipid peroxidation during refractory status epilepticus. Traces the cascade from NMDA receptor-mediated excitotoxicity to the catastrophic collapse of neuronal membrane integrity, linking oxidative stress to the irreversible metabolic failure seen in clinical coma.

episodes.label: Tears, Stria Melanocytes, and Spinal Arcs — Veterinary Ophthalmic Exam, Descemetocele 'Donut Hole' & TonoVet Physics (V033), BAER Deafness Screening, MITF/PMEL Stria Collapse & Cavalier PSOM (V034) & Neurologic Localization, Schiff-Sherrington & the Deep Pain Law (V035)
episodes.notes: One Medicine synthesis of veterinary ophthalmology/tonometry (V033), BAER deafness screening (V034), and neurologic localization (V035): STT-I sequence, cherry-eye gland preservation, descemetocele fluorescein 'donut hole', collar/species TonoVet traps, and fellow-eye glaucoma prophylaxis; Strain's >12,000 Dalmatian registry, MITF/KIT stria melanocytes, OFA >=35d rule, and Cavalier PSOM bone BAER; and 4 spinal segments, Schiff-Sherrington, paradoxical vestibular tilt, and Olby's Deep Pain & Progressive Myelomalacia laws.

episodes.label: Decibels, Diopters, and Millimeters of Mercury — Audiometry, Shadow-Curve Masking, SSCD & NICU ANSD (H050), ETDRS Acuity, Pinhole Optics & Cycloplegic Refraction (H051) & Goldmann 3.06 mm Tonometry, OHTS & Normal-Tension Glaucoma (H052)
episodes.notes: Clinical Cluster & Sensory Biophysics synthesis of audiometry (H050), visual acuity/refraction (H051), and tonometry (H052): unmasked shadow curves, 2 kHz Carhart notch, schwannoma WRS rollover, SSCD stapedial reflex rescue, and NICU OAE+/ABR- ANSD; ETDRS LogMAR, paradoxical pinhole worsening, cycloplegic pseudomyopia, and 20/20 bitemporal hemianopia; and Goldmann 3.06 mm physics, OHTS CCT, post-LASIK PISK, and Tajimi/CNTGS Normal-Tension Glaucoma.

episodes.label: Epochs, Dipoles, and Saltatory Sparks — Attended Polysomnography, Hypopnea Rules & HSAT Dilution (H044), Scalp & ICU Continuous EEG (H045) & Nerve Conduction Studies and Needle EMG (H046)
episodes.notes: Clinical Cluster & Neurophysiology synthesis of attended polysomnography (H044), scalp/ICU EEG (H045), and NCS/needle EMG (H046): 3% vs. 4% hypopnea rules, pediatric >=2-breath cutoffs, HSAT TRT dilution, RBD synucleinopathy, and CHAT (n=464); 6-10 cm2 cortical dipole threshold, wicket-spike traps, Claassen ICU cEEG (n=570, 92% non-convulsive), and TELSTAR (n=172); and small-fiber blindness, the DRG SNAP law, 10-21 day Wallerian clock, MG vs. LEMS facilitation, cool-limb sodium physics, Martin-Gruber, and Gold Coast ALS criteria.

episodes.label: Locked In Syndrome and the Sodium Correction Trap
episodes.notes: Bioinorganic and clinical neurology analysis of locked-in syndrome resulting from osmotic demyelination syndrome during chronic hyponatremia correction. Traces how rapid serum sodium elevation dehydrates pontine oligodendrocytes, requiring immediate therapeutic re-lowering via D5W and desmopressin protocols.

episodes.label: How a Sleeping Pill Woke a Silent Brain
episodes.notes: Neuropharmacological dissection of the zolpidem paradox, where a sedative-hypnotic agent restores consciousness in patients with severe brain injury. Examines the biophysical mechanisms of thalamic deep brain stimulation alongside GABAergic modulation to resolve the clinical mysteries of the "found down" patient and the recovery of the silent brain.

episodes.label: Propofol Alpha Cages Versus Ketamine Dissociative Dreams
episodes.notes: Neuropharmacological and electrophysiological comparison of propofol-induced cortical alpha oscillations and ketamine-mediated dissociative dream states. Analyzes quantitative electroencephalographic indices of consciousness and connectivity during targeted general anesthesia and altered state paradigms.

episodes.label: Anosognosia and How Stroke Erases Half of Reality
episodes.notes: Neurological and neuropsychological investigation of anosognosia and right temporal-parietal junction stroke leading to left-sided neglect. Explores how acute focal brain lesions disrupt internal body schema representation, causing patients to vehemently deny paralysis and perceptual deficits.

episodes.label: Invisible ICU Seizures and the Thiamine Dextrose Trap
episodes.notes: Clinical and biochemical reconstruction of non-convulsive status epilepticus and the iatrogenic risks of the thiamine-dextrose trap in the intensive care unit. Examines the pathophysiology of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome alongside the diagnostic challenges of silent seizures in patients presenting with altered consciousness.

episodes.label: The Click That Mapped the Room — Human Mouth-Click Echolocation Acoustics, Calcarine V1 Recruitment in Blind Experts (Thaler 2011), 10-Week Novice Training & Echo EEG
episodes.notes: Acoustics and cross-modal cortical plasticity of human mouth-click echolocation: Thaler et al.'s (2017) beam-pattern and millisecond click measurements, Thaler et al.'s (2011) fMRI demonstration of calcarine visual-cortex echo-specific BOLD modulation in blind echolocators, Norman et al.'s (2021) 20-session training of blind and sighted novices across adulthood, and Garcia-Lazaro et al.'s (2026) EEG echo-evidence accumulation.

episodes.label: The Odor They Learned to Detect — Unilateral Nostril Androstenone Induction (Mainland 2002), Human OR7D4 Genetic Polymorphisms (Keller 2007) & Olfactory Training
episodes.notes: Peripheral vs. central plasticity in human olfaction: Mainland et al.'s (2002) single-nostril exposure experiment showing contralateral transfer of acquired androstenone sensitivity, Keller et al.'s (2007) and Lunde et al.'s (2012) OR7D4 RT/WM receptor variants governing odor intensity and valence in pork taint, and Gillmeister et al.'s (2025) olfactory perceptual training.

episodes.label: The Signal the Poison Interrupted — Delayed Belladonna Atropine Rebound via LC-MS/MS, Scopolamine Hippocampal Theta Disruption & Physostigmine vs. Lorazepam in Antimuscarinic Delirium
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of central and peripheral muscarinic blockade: delayed gastrointestinal absorption and day-4 LC-MS/MS serum atropine rebound after belladonna ingestion (Hayashi et al. 2026), human intracranial EEG evidence of scopolamine disrupting hippocampal theta oscillations during memory encoding (Gedankien et al. 2023), and randomized trial evidence comparing physostigmine cholinesterase inhibition against lorazepam sedation in antimuscarinic delirium.

episodes.label: The Sedative You Can Wake From — Dexmedetomidine Locus Coeruleus Alpha-2A Cryo-EM, GIRK Hyperpolarization, Vascular vs. Sympatholytic Biphasic Pressure & SPICE III / MENDS2 Trials
episodes.notes: Molecular and critical-care pharmacology of dexmedetomidine: chiral resolution of medetomidine into its active S/d-enantiomer (1990), locus coeruleus alpha-2A Gi/o-GIRK hyperpolarization and sleep-pathway disinhibition vs. GABA-A coma, human alpha-2A cryo-EM binding pocket geometry, biphasic peripheral alpha-2B vasoconstriction vs. central sympatholysis, and the MENDS, MIDEX/PRODEX, SPICE III, and MENDS2 clinical trials.

episodes.label: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

episodes.label: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
episodes.notes: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

episodes.label: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
episodes.notes: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
episodes.notes: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

episodes.label: The Breakfast That Changed a Bargain — Controlled 850-kcal Breakfast Crossovers in Ultimatum Bargaining (Strang 2017) vs. fMRI Risk Lotteries (Liu 2021), Plasma Tyrosine/LNAA & Human Tyrosine Hydroxylase Cryo-EM (6ZZU/6ZVP)
episodes.notes: How acute macronutrient swaps in controlled 850-kcal breakfasts affect distinct economic decision tasks: Strang et al.'s (2017) Ultimatum Game crossover (unfair-offer rejection and plasma tyrosine/LNAA AUC) vs. Liu et al.'s (2021) fMRI monetary lottery crossover (overall behavioral null, fat-mass interaction, tryptophan/LNAA correlation, and parietal BOLD thresholds), grounded in human tyrosine hydroxylase cryo-EM structures (PDB 6ZZU apo & 6ZVP dopamine-bound).

episodes.label: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
episodes.notes: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

episodes.label: When the Brain Burns Ketones — Drug-Resistant Pediatric Epilepsy, SCOT Succinyl-CoA Transferase (3DLX / 1OOY), [11C]Acetoacetate PET, Decanoate AMPA Block & the Neal Trial
episodes.notes: From the 4:1 ketogenic diet ratio (90% energy from fat) and hepatic HMGCS2 ketogenesis to extrahepatic SCOT/OXCT1 glutamyl-CoA thioester catalysis (human apo PDB 3DLX vs. porcine Glu305 intermediate PDB 1OOY), dual [11C]acetoacetate/[18F]FDG brain PET, Chang et al. (2016) decanoic acid GluA2/GluA3 AMPA receptor antagonism, and Neal et al.'s (2008) randomized childhood epilepsy trial (145 randomized, 103 analyzed at 3 months).

episodes.label: The Side the Scalp Could See — Simultaneous Scalp vs. Stereo-EEG Seizure Detection (Gunnell 2025), 51-Second Contralateral Scalp Lag & ICU Peripheral Nerve Stimulator EEG Artifacts
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain of clinical electroencephalography (H045): simultaneous intracranial stereo-EEG and scalp EEG recordings showing a 51-second delay and false contralateral lateralization on the scalp (Nandkeolyar 2018; Gunnell et al. 2025 across 172 seizures), skull/tissue attenuation of deep focal discharges, and ICU peripheral nerve stimulator train-of-four artifacts mimicking seizures (Dhakal 2017).

episodes.label: The Pause That Finally Had a Time — Implantable Loop Recorder Asystole Masquerading as Epilepsy (Kanjwal 2010) vs. 38-Second Ictal Asystole on Simultaneous EEG/ECG (Nandkeolyar 2018), RAST Yield & Recorder Artifacts
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain of ambulatory ECG and implantable loop recording (H041): Kanjwal et al.'s (2010) loop-recorder capture of complete heart block and prolonged asystole causing convulsive syncope previously treated as epilepsy, contrasted with Nandkeolyar et al.'s (2018) simultaneous video-EEG/ECG capture of right temporal seizure onset preceding a 38-second ictal asystole, Krahn's randomized RAST diagnostic yield (14/27 vs. 6/30), and Domenichini's (2023) false-positive pause artifacts.

episodes.label: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

episodes.label: The Click With No Trace — Canine Unilateral BAER Deafness (Plonek English Setter & Lewis 8,955 UK Dalmatians) vs. Pediatric Auditory Neuropathy Recovery with Normal Speech & Absent Click ABR
episodes.notes: Comparative auditory diagnostics across species (H050 & V034): Plonek's unilaterally deaf English Setter BAER waveforms and Lewis's 8,955-dog UK Dalmatian screening cohort (1,201 unilateral, 397 bilateral, 8 equivocal) paired with Starr's classic auditory neuropathy series and Eom's child with absent click ABR yet normal pure-tone thresholds and language.

episodes.label: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
episodes.notes: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

episodes.label: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
episodes.notes: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

episodes.label: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
episodes.notes: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

episodes.label: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
episodes.notes: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

episodes.label: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
episodes.notes: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

episodes.label: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

episodes.label: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
episodes.notes: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

episodes.label: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
episodes.notes: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

episodes.label: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
episodes.notes: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

episodes.label: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
episodes.notes: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

episodes.label: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
episodes.notes: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

episodes.label: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
episodes.notes: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

episodes.label: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
episodes.notes: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

episodes.label: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
episodes.notes: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

episodes.label: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
episodes.notes: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

episodes.label: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
episodes.notes: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

episodes.label: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
episodes.notes: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

episodes.label: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
episodes.notes: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

episodes.label: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
episodes.notes: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

episodes.label: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
episodes.notes: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

episodes.label: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

episodes.label: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
episodes.notes: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

episodes.label: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
episodes.notes: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

episodes.label: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
episodes.notes: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

episodes.label: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
episodes.notes: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

episodes.label: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
episodes.notes: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

episodes.label: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
episodes.notes: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

episodes.label: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
episodes.notes: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

episodes.label: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
episodes.notes: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

episodes.label: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
episodes.notes: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

episodes.label: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
episodes.notes: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

episodes.label: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
episodes.notes: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

episodes.label: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
episodes.notes: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

episodes.label: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
episodes.notes: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

episodes.label: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
episodes.notes: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.

episodes.label: How Living Cells Think With Electricity
episodes.notes: Mechanistic synthesis of the bioelectric dynasty, from Hodgkin and Huxley’s squid giant axon voltage clamps to Jens Christian Skou’s isolation of Na+/K+-ATPase from 25,000 shore crabs. Traces the evolution of patch-clamp electrophysiology through the KcsA selectivity filter and the 100-gigaohm resolution of single-channel molecular gating.

episodes.label: Why Your Brain Runs on 20 Watts
episodes.notes: Thermodynamic and enzymatic audit of the human brain’s 20-watt power budget, focusing on Attwell and Laughlin’s action-potential ATP calculations. Examines the role of B-vitamin coenzymes and astrocyte-neuron lactate shuttling alongside the biophysics of active ATP-hydrotropism within biomolecular condensates to maintain neural homeostasis.

episodes.label: Cognitive Enhancement Is Not Consciousness Enhancement
episodes.notes: Neurobiological critique of the hardware-centric metaphor for cognitive optimization, contrasting linear computational metrics like RAM and processing speed with the non-linear biophysics of subjective awareness. Argues that synaptic scaling and neural computation cannot be reduced to simple numerical upgrades without addressing qualia.

episodes.label: How Biology Turns Physics into Reality
episodes.notes: Biophysical resolution of how the central nervous system translates exogenous mechanical and electromagnetic energy into uniform electrical impulses to construct a coherent subjective reality. Examines the neurobiological hallucination of the external world, where chaotic environmental stimuli are filtered to generate phenomenological perception.

episodes.label: The Atomic Mechanics of Neural Signals
episodes.notes: Biophysical and electrophysiological resolution of synaptic transmission, focusing on the protein motors and 60-millivolt electrical triggers that govern neurotransmitter release. Integrates the 1996 Arnold Starr findings on auditory neuropathy to model how desynchronized neural signals disrupt sensory reality at the atomic and cellular level.

episodes.label: An Omega-3's Journey to a Human Thought
episodes.notes: Molecular dynamic simulation of a polyunsaturated fatty acid’s transit from dietary ingestion to synaptic integration within the human central nervous system. Traces the biochemical odyssey through the vascular endothelium and blood-brain barrier to elucidate the biophysical role of lipids in modulating cognitive architecture.

episodes.label: How Cognitive Bottlenecks Limit Consciousness
episodes.notes: Neurocomputational and biophysical analysis of sensory processing bottlenecks that constrain conscious human perception. Explores how neural architectures operate near mechanical limits to maintain the cohesive illusion of a continuous, movie-like external reality.

episodes.label: How Neurons Fuel Their Synapses
episodes.notes: Bioenergetic and electrophysiological analysis of mitochondrial ATP delivery and the metabolic costs of chemical neurotransmission. Explores the paradigm shift of cancer neuroscience, specifically how CaV3.1 window currents fuel the formation of functional glutamatergic synapses between neurons and high-grade gliomas to drive malignant progression.

episodes.label: How Brains Turn Voltage Into Reality
episodes.notes: Biophysical and neurophysiological analysis of action potentials, ion channel gating, and how microvoltage oscillations construct conscious sensory reality. Examines the membrane capacitance and electrochemical gradient mechanisms translating neural electrical signals into subjective human experience.

episodes.label: How Thirteen Watts Shapes Human Consciousness
episodes.notes: Energetic and evolutionary audit of the human brain’s 13-watt power consumption and its role in generating rich phenomenological awareness. Synthesizes the biophysics of neural efficiency with the adaptive intelligence required for the Agricultural Revolution, highlighting how complex problem-solving emerged within strict metabolic constraints.

episodes.label: How Brains Construct Reality From Physics
episodes.notes: Computational and neurobiological analysis of predictive processing and the role of sensory priors in generating perceived reality. Examines how the brain utilizes inferential models to synthesize raw physical data into a coherent internal representation, bridging the gap between synaptic biophysics and the subjective experience of consciousness.

episodes.label: The Electrical Signature of Human Consciousness
episodes.notes: Electrophysiological examination of human consciousness and cortical information processing. Evaluates EEG gamma synchrony, global workspace ignition models, and the distinct electromagnetic field correlates underlying subjective sensory awareness.

episodes.label: How Sensory Transduction Constructs Reality
episodes.notes: Biophysical and philological investigation of how sensory transduction co-constructs clinical reality, from cochlear hair cell deflection to S-cone activation. Analyzes how ancient lexicons partitioned visual experience based on luster and motion rather than abstract hue, demonstrating the interplay between raw physics and linguistic framing.

episodes.label: The Biophysics of a Single Thought
episodes.notes: Biophysical resolution of molecular signaling cascades and dendritic integration within individual cortical assemblies. Analyzes how synaptic plasticity and neural computation transform raw sensory reality into embodied consciousness through precise spatiotemporal electrochemical transitions across the synaptic cleft.

episodes.label: How Brains Create Conscious Experience
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of the "hard problem" of consciousness through the lens of recurrent processing theory and integrated information dynamics. Analyzes the biophysical transition from synaptic signaling to subjective qualia, examining how neural architectures synthesize raw sensory data into embodied reality.

episodes.label: How Your Brain Constructs Reality
episodes.notes: Epistemological and neurocomputational analysis of predictive processing in the brain. Investigates active inference frameworks, Helmholtzian unconscious inference, and the hierarchical generation of conscious perceptual reality.

episodes.label: How the Brain Manufactures Suffering
episodes.notes: Neuroanatomical and psychological dissection of affective suffering versus basic nociception. Examines functional magnetic resonance imaging correlates within the anterior cingulate cortex, insular cortex, and descending modulatory pathways.

episodes.label: How Anxiety Amplifies Physical Pain
episodes.notes: Clinical neurobiological and pharmacological investigation of persistent nociceptive signaling, examining how central anxiety circuits modulate pain perception. Evaluates therapeutic NAV1.8 voltage-gated sodium channel inhibitors against chronic pain pathology to unpack the physiological burden on healthcare systems.

sections.heading: Living Human Neurons, Artificial Neural Networks & Valuation

episodes.label: The Gorilla in the Scan — Radiologist Chest-CT Inattentional Blindness With Direct Gaze Fixation (Drew 2013), Simons & Chabris (1999), Fast-Motion Limits & Perceptual Sensitivity
episodes.notes: Visual attention, expert search, and perceptual awareness boundaries: Simons & Chabris's (1999) selective-attention paradigm, Drew et al.'s (2013) lung-nodule chest-CT experiment in which 20 of 24 radiologists missed an embedded gorilla despite majority eye-tracking fixation on its location, Wallisch et al.'s (2023) motion-speed boundary conditions, and Nartker et al.'s (2025) large-scale test of residual visual sensitivity.

episodes.label: How Living Human Neurons Outcompute Supercomputers
episodes.notes: Neurocomputational comparison of biological cortical circuits against deep convolutional neural networks. Analyzes how living primate visual cortex utilizes massive descending recurrent feedback and V2/V4 border-ownership neurons to outperform artificial hierarchies that lack holistic object representation.

episodes.label: Why Neural Networks Are Not Brains
episodes.notes: Neurobiological and computational critique of the structural divergence between artificial neural networks and biological nervous systems, exemplified by the fused syncytial web of Ctenophora. Contrasts the discrete synaptic architecture of mammalian brains with the statistical heuristics of large language models to define intelligence.

episodes.label: How Neural Networks Mirror Human Brains
episodes.notes: Computational and neurobiological audit of the structural parallels between biological neurons and billion-parameter evolutionary protein-language transformers. Evaluates the mathematics of consciousness and Bayesian priors in neural architectures to assign pathogenicity scores across the human proteome using sequence-based convolutional networks.

episodes.label: Why Economists Ignore the Human Brain
episodes.notes: Neuroeconomic and behavioral audit of the discrepancy between hyper-rational utility maximization models and actual human decision-making in gym membership commitment. Analyzes the failure of standard economic frameworks to account for neural valuation and the biological constraints that drive irrational behavioral patterns despite stated intentions.

episodes.notes: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

episodes.notes: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

episodes.notes: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

episodes.label: 31,000 Years Before Anesthesia: Borneo Cave Amputation & Pleistocene Care
episodes.notes: Archaeopathological and bioarchaeological investigation of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo tibial-fibular surgical amputation in Borneo. Synthesizes prehistoric paleosurgery evidence with Shanidar 1 skeletal trauma, Pleistocene care dynamics, and ancestral plant-derived zoopharmacognosy.

episodes.label: How Monoclonal Antibodies Trigger Immune Self-Destruction
episodes.notes: Immunological and toxicological dissection of engineered CD28 superagonist monoclonal antibodies that bypass T-cell co-stimulation checkpoints to unleash catastrophic cytokine release syndrome. Reconstructs how species-specific Fc and memory-T-cell differences turned preclinical safety models into acute multi-organ failure.

episodes.label: How Soviet Mint Drops Triggered Seizures
episodes.notes: Clinical and neuropharmacological dissection of covert barbiturate withdrawal seizures triggered by abrupt discontinuation of Soviet peppermint drops (Corvalol) alongside porcine Cerebrolysin therapy. Traces hidden phenobarbital and ethyl bromoisovalerate GABA-A receptor dependence behind iatrogenic status epilepticus.

episodes.label: How a Fever Suppository Caused Organ Failure
episodes.notes: Toxicologic and forensic audit of pediatric organ failure following the administration of rectal antipyretic suppositories for routine fever management. Compares international clinical protocols between the US and France to identify the biochemical triggers and metabolic traps that convert common pediatric interventions into systemic catastrophes.

episodes.label: How the Brain Survives a Seizure
episodes.notes: Cellular and metabolic investigation of prolonged epileptic seizure termination. Analyzes inhibitory interneuron GABAergic signaling, ATP depletion thresholds, excitotoxic calcium loading, and emergency neurovascular restorative coupling.

episodes.label: Sacred Bark, Blowgun Curare & Sleeping Sponges to Modern Anesthesia
episodes.notes: Pharmacological and archaeomedical reconstruction of the lineage from ancient botanical toxins to modern balanced anesthesia. Traces the receptor-level transition from Amazonian curare-induced neuromuscular blockade and medieval spongia somnifera to the refined application of sodium-channel blockers and alkaloids in contemporary surgical practice.

episodes.label: Surviving Malignant Hyperthermia and Anesthetic Toxicity
episodes.notes: Pharmacological and clinical investigation of life-threatening anesthetic toxicities, focusing on ryanodine receptor mutations driving malignant hyperthermia. Analyzes the molecular mechanisms of core body temperature escalation, metabolic collapse, and rapid-onset cardiovascular arrest during surgical procedures.

episodes.label: When Targeted Drugs Trigger Systemic Collapse
episodes.notes: Pharmacodynamic dissection of targeted biologic therapies and systemic inflammatory collapse. Examines how exogenous molecular agents disrupt complex homeostatic feedback networks and trigger severe immunogenic toxicities.

episodes.label: Why Common Diabetes Pills Turn Deadly
episodes.notes: Clinical and biochemical reconstruction of metabolic toxicology where homeostatic rebellion transforms common antidiabetic agents into lethal hazards. Investigates how dehydration and environmental shifts disrupt drug clearance mechanisms, leading to catastrophic failures in dynamic equilibrium and the forensic markers of insulin-related crises.
